text:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT PAGE: High error rate and elevated p95 latency observed in us-east (us-east-1). Traffic is failing over to us-west (us-west-2) and eu-central, creating health-check flipflop across regions. Paging oncall. Impact: increased 5xx and degraded throughput for inference endpoints. Links: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/abcd/region-health ?orgId=1 :rotating_light:

irina: acked. oncall here, pulling logs. seeing rapid 502 spikes from router when failover happens.

sam: timeline - started ~2557777900. us-east host pool started returning 502s, router sent traffic to us-west. us-west has different model variant (v4-quant) vs us-east (v3-int8). suspect model-variant incompat leads to KV cache misses and OOMs on warmups.

mike: confirm logs show "kv-cache: version mismatch" on some us-west pods. grep: 
``` 
2026-03-10T12:24:05Z router[us-west] WARN kv-cache: incompatible-metadata v3 vs v4
2026-03-10T12:24:06Z model[us-west]/pod-13 ERROR OOM while warming kv cache
```

david: that would explain slow warmups causing healthchecks to fail and router flapping back -> oscillation. customers behind sticky routing see 500s.

carol: customer-impact quick scan: 12 tenants with retry loops hit; 2 enterprise accounts reported sustained 30% error rate for sync endpoints. We should notify CSMs asap.

irina: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable cross-region automatic fallback in routing-policy for affected load-balancers, 2) pin affected customer routes to their local region, 3) rollback us-west model variant to v3-int8 OR remove kv-cache compatibility flag in runtime until model onboarding patch. Which is faster?

sam: disabling fallback is fast. rollback model will require deploy (~10-15m) and may cause rolling restarts. I'd do disable fallback + scale up us-east replicas first.

mike: set routing-policy: 
```
POST /api/v1/routing-policies/region-fallback/modify
{ "allow_cross_region_fallback": false, "affected_pools": ["router-prod-us-east-1"] }
```

ops-bot: ACTION: routing-policy updated by sam at 2557778020. allow_cross_region_fallback=false :white_check_mark:

sam: scaling us-east pool +20% now. applying: `kubectl scale deployment/inference-pool-us-east --replicas=18`

david: rolling verify: traces show fewer 502s post-policy-change; however some customers still see errors due to in-flight sessions pinned to failing pods. need drain.

carol: CSM notify draft: "We're aware of intermittent 5xx for inference in US region. We've temporarily disabled cross-region failover while we stabilize model variants. Expect progressive recovery in next 15-30m. Your sessions might require retries." Approve? :thinking_face:

irina: send. cc:security, CSMs.

sam: triggering emergency rollback of us-west model to v3-int8 as a follow-up. kicking off deploy at 2557778105.

mike: deploy logs:
```
Deploy v3-int8 -> us-west started @2557778105
Pod replacement pod-13 -> pod-13-rollback succeeded @2557778189
All us-west pods reporting kv-cache OK @2557778205
```

ops-bot: CHECK: healthchecks passing across regions at 2557778220. Cross-region flapping no longer observed. allow_cross_region_fallback still false until we verify.

david: metrics: error rate down from 18% -> 2% over last 5m; p95 latency back to baseline. Confirming customer impact reduced.

carol: CSM update sent at 2557778230. Two enterprise customers acknowledged and will retry.

irina: root-cause hypothesis: model onboarding pipeline allowed v4-quant (breaking KV-cache metadata change) to roll into us-west pool without compatibility flag. When heat/scale caused slow warmups OOMs, healthchecks tripped and router attempted cross-region fallback; because us-east and us-west had divergent model variants, warmup/compat issues amplified the failover loop.

sam: immediate next-steps (short): 1) re-enable fallback only after canary run and compatibility check, 2) add gating in rollout to block incompatible KV-metadata changes, 3) add router debounce (10s) to health-failover to reduce oscillation.

mike: long-term: model-variant compatibility tests in CI, explicit kv-cache versioning header on model artifacts, auto-pin policy for mixed-variant rollouts.

irina: doc the incident and assign postmortem owners. postmortem ticket: PM-7021. Owner: sam. Expected draft in 48h.

ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: incident cleared at 2557778287. Root-cause mitigated, customers recovering. Pager duty: close once postmortem filed. :tada:

carol: thanks team. I'll keep monitoring for 1 hour and then slack update before closing channel.

irina: good work, quick mitigation. adding notes to oncall-runbook about disabling fallback during model rollout anomalies.

sam: adding follow-up PRs now.

mike: closing window of noisy alerts. please ping if any regression.
